name: Bachalpsee from First
trending_reason: The Schreckhorn and Wetterhorn mirrored in an alpine lake; one of Switzerland’s most photographed spots
blurb: An easy path from First to the Bachalpsee, where the Schreckhorn and Wetterhorn reflect in the still water.
description: From the First gondola station above Grindelwald, a wide, easy path climbs gently for about an hour to the Bachalpsee at 2,265 m, where the Schreckhorn and Wetterhorn reflect in the water on a calm morning. Fine for families; carry on up to the Faulhorn, or try the First Cliff Walk platform by the gondola station.

name: Faulhorn Traverse (First → Schynige Platte)
access: Gondola to First; back on the Schynige Platte railway (summer only)
trending_reason: Lonely Planet’s best day hike for taking in the Bernese Oberland
blurb: A high traverse past the Bachalpsee to the summit hotel on the Faulhorn and along the ridge to Schynige Platte, facing the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau all day.
description: A classic Bernese Oberland traverse: from First past the Bachalpsee to the summit of the Faulhorn (2,681 m), crowned by a mountain hotel from 1830, then along the ridge to Schynige Platte. The Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau face you all day, with Lake Brienz below on the other side. A long but non-technical day; return on the Schynige Platte cog railway, which runs in summer only.

name: Eiger Trail
access: Jungfrau railway to Eigergletscher; train back from Alpiglen
trending_reason: Walk the foot of the Eiger north face, one of the most famous walls in climbing
blurb: A mostly downhill path right along the foot of the Eiger north face, from the Eigergletscher station to Alpiglen.
description: A mostly downhill path from the Eigergletscher station of the Jungfrau Railway, right along the foot of the Eiger north face to Alpiglen. You walk beneath the 1,800 m wall where climbing history was written, with views across to Grindelwald and the Wetterhorn. About two hours; take the train up from Kleine Scheidegg and back down from Alpiglen.

name: 5-Seenweg (Five Lakes Walk)
access: Sunnegga funicular and Blauherd gondola from Zermatt; back down from Sunnegga
trending_reason: The Matterhorn reflected in the Stellisee is one of the most-shared views in the Alps
blurb: From Blauherd past the Stellisee, Grindjisee, Grünsee, Moosjisee and Leisee, with the Matterhorn mirrored in the water on a calm morning.
description: From Blauherd above Zermatt, the 5-Seenweg strings together five small mountain lakes, the Stellisee, Grindjisee, Grünsee, Moosjisee and Leisee, with the Matterhorn reflected in several of them on a calm morning. The path is well marked and mostly downhill; finish at the Leisee by the Sunnegga funicular, which has a little beach for children. Early starts give the stillest water.

name: Riffelsee Matterhorn Reflection
access: Gornergrat railway to Rotenboden; back from Riffelberg
blurb: Step off the Gornergrat railway at Rotenboden and walk down past the Riffelsee, where the Matterhorn mirrors in the water, to Riffelberg.
description: Step off the Gornergrat railway at Rotenboden and walk a few minutes down to the Riffelsee, where the Matterhorn mirrors in the water: the classic Zermatt photo. Carry on gently down to Riffelberg for the train back, or ride up to the Gornergrat first for the Gorner glacier and Monte Rosa. Calm mornings give the best reflection.

name: Hörnlihütte from Schwarzsee
access: Matterhorn Express gondola from Zermatt to Schwarzsee
access_note: Hut open mid-June to mid-September; fixed-rope sections (SAC T3–T4).
trending_reason: Base camp of the Matterhorn’s Hörnli ridge, the most famous climbing route in the Alps
blurb: A steep, rocky climb with fixed ropes up the Hörnli ridge to the Matterhorn base camp at 3,260 m, as close as hikers get.
description: The closest most hikers get to the Matterhorn: from Schwarzsee the trail climbs the Hörnli ridge to the Hörnlihütte at 3,260 m, base camp of the classic climbing route to the summit. The upper part is steep and rocky with fixed ropes and steps (SAC T3–T4), and the altitude is noticeable. The hut serves food from mid-June to mid-September.

name: Oeschinensee Panorama Loop
access_note: A rockfall from the Spitze Stei on 8 Aug 2026 did not reach visitor areas; the south-west end of the lake has been closed since 2019.
trending_reason: Glacier-fed turquoise lake under the Blüemlisalp; heavily shared aerial and lakeside shots
blurb: From the gondola to the lake and up the panorama trail on the north slope, for the famous view down onto the turquoise water and the Blüemlisalp.
description: A gondola from Kandersteg puts you a short walk from the Oeschinensee, a glacier-fed turquoise lake under the cliffs of the Blüemlisalp, part of the Jungfrau-Aletsch World Heritage site. The panorama loop climbs the north slope to the Heuberg for the famous view down onto the water, then returns along the shore; some steep, narrow sections need sure footing.

name: Harder Kulm on Foot
access: Up on foot from Interlaken; down on the Harderbahn funicular
trending_reason: The Two Lakes Bridge platform high above Interlaken
blurb: A steep forest climb from Interlaken to the Harder Kulm restaurant and Two Lakes Bridge, above Lake Thun and Lake Brienz with the Jungfrau opposite.
description: Interlaken’s house mountain: a steep forest path climbs about 780 m from town to the Harder Kulm restaurant at 1,322 m, where the Two Lakes Bridge platform hangs over the slope with Lake Thun on one side, Lake Brienz on the other and the Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau straight ahead. Ride the Harderbahn funicular back down.

name: Brunni Trail to the Härzlisee
access: Up on foot from Engelberg, or the Brunni cable car and chairlift; ride down
trending_reason: The heart-shaped lake with a barefoot path, popular on family reels
blurb: Climb from Engelberg to the Brunnihütte and the little heart-shaped Härzlisee, with a barefoot path round it and the Titlis across the valley.
description: From Engelberg the Brunni-Trail climbs steeply through meadows and forest to the Brunnihütte and the Härzlisee, a small heart-shaped lake with a barefoot path round it and the Titlis glaciers across the valley. Too steep? The Brunni cable car and chairlift do most of the climb and leave an easy family walk at the top.

name: Seealpsee, Aescher & Ebenalp
access: Appenzell railway to Wasserauen; Ebenalp cable car back down
trending_reason: The cliff-hugging Aescher guesthouse is one of Switzerland’s most shared images
blurb: From Wasserauen up to the Seealpsee, then steeply to the Aescher guesthouse wedged under its cliff, the Wildkirchli caves and the Ebenalp.
description: Appenzell’s classic: from Wasserauen up to the Seealpsee, then a steep climb to the Aescher, the guesthouse built into the cliff, and through the Wildkirchli caves, once home to hermits and long before that to cave bears, to the Ebenalp. Ride the cable car back down. The path below the Aescher is steep and exposed in places, and very busy on summer weekends.

name: Rigi Kaltbad to Rigi Kulm
access: Cog railway from Vitznau or Arth-Goldau, or the cable car from Weggis
trending_reason: The “Queen of the Mountains” panorama over Lake Lucerne
blurb: An easy walk to the summit of the Rigi, with Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and the Alps from the Säntis to the Jungfrau around you.
description: An easy walk from Rigi Kaltbad up to the 1,797 m summit of the “Queen of the Mountains”, with Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and a long line of Alps from the Säntis to the Jungfrau around you. Europe’s first mountain railway (1871) climbs from Vitznau, a second from Arth-Goldau, and a cable car runs from Weggis to Kaltbad.

name: Aletsch Panorama Trail
access: Cable car from Riederalp to Moosfluh
trending_reason: The longest glacier in the Alps, a UNESCO World Heritage site
blurb: From the Moosfluh viewpoint above the Great Aletsch Glacier, the longest in the Alps, along the ridge to Riederfurka and down to Riederalp.
description: From the Moosfluh viewpoint above Riederalp you look straight down onto the Great Aletsch Glacier, the longest in the Alps, curving some 20 km down from the Jungfrau. The trail follows the ridge to the Riederfurka, then drops gently to Riederalp; the Moosfluh slope itself is slowly sliding, so follow any signed diversions. The whole plateau is car-free, reached by cable car from the Rhône valley.

name: Verzasca Valley & Ponte dei Salti
access: Bus from Locarno to Lavertezzo Paese
trending_reason: The double-arched stone bridge over emerald water is a Ticino icon
blurb: A riverside path up the Verzasca from the double-arched Ponte dei Salti, past emerald pools and smooth granite slabs.
description: At Lavertezzo the double-arched stone Ponte dei Salti spans emerald pools and smooth granite slabs: Ticino’s most photographed river scene. The valley path follows the Verzasca upstream through chestnut woods and stone hamlets; walk as far as you like and return the same way. The water is cold and fast, so swim only in calm pools and stay out after rain.

name: Lauterbrunnen Valley Walk
access: Train to Lauterbrunnen; PostBus back from Stechelberg
access_note: Trümmelbach Falls entry about CHF 18; open April to early November.
trending_reason: The valley of 72 waterfalls under sheer cliffs, an endlessly shared Swiss scene
blurb: A flat valley-floor walk past the Staubbach Falls to the glacier-fed Trümmelbach Falls inside the cliff, and on to Stechelberg.
description: A flat walk along the floor of the Lauterbrunnen valley, past the 300 m Staubbach Falls and beneath sheer cliffs streaked with waterfalls, to the Trümmelbach Falls: ten glacier-fed falls thundering inside the mountain, reached by a tunnel lift (admission, April to early November). Continue to Stechelberg and take the PostBus back.

name: Walker’s Haute Route
access: Train to Chamonix; train home from Zermatt
trending_reason: The classic glacier-free route between the two great Alpine resorts
blurb: From Chamonix to Zermatt over a string of high passes between Mont Blanc and the Matterhorn: glacier-free, but long and high.
description: The walker’s route between the two great Alpine resorts: about 210 km from Chamonix to Zermatt in 12–14 days, over a string of high passes up to the Col de Prafleuri (2,987 m) and through Champex, Arolla and Zinal. The standard variants avoid glaciers, but expect long days, around 14,000 m of ascent in total and a few steep, exposed passes. Mont Blanc at the start, the Matterhorn at the end.

name: Tour du Mont Blanc
access: Bus or train from Chamonix to Les Houches
access_note: From 2027 the French communes plan to require a booked bed every night and ban bivouacs; Refuge de la Croix du Bonhomme closes after mid-August 2026 for renovation (reopening about 2029).
trending_reason: The most famous multi-day walk in the Alps
blurb: An 11-stage loop round the Mont Blanc massif through France, Italy and Switzerland, with a glacier view from nearly every pass.
description: The most famous multi-day walk in the Alps: a 170 km loop round the Mont Blanc massif through France, Italy and Switzerland, traditionally anti-clockwise from Les Houches in about 11 stages. Huts, hotels and villages break up long days with around 10,000 m of ascent; the high point of the standard route is the Grand Col Ferret (2,537 m). Book beds well ahead: from 2027 the French communes plan to require a booked bed every night.
